clue.text: Company satisfied with one's rubbish mobile being returned, as special purchase

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it
one's = one is, so I + S
rot = nonsense, rubbish
a cell (phone) is a mobile

explanation.surface: A firm pleased to be sent back a scrapped phone, treating it as a prized acquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the four pieces after 'Company' are turned round; CO stays where it is at the front. 'Mobile' is a noun here, the phone, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector's item is something bought because it is rare or special.

clue.text: German agreed to get French right on board

indicators.note: placed right on something is set immediately beside it

parts.note: the French word for yes
German for yes, placed right on (immediately after) the French

explanation.surface: A German agrees to bring a French speaker properly into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouija board's name is itself French yes plus German yes, so the wordplay retells the word's origin. 'On board' looks like a phrase meaning 'in agreement', but 'board' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is the lettered board used at seances.

clue.text: Looked unpleasantly twisted when swapping sides

indicators.note: sides are left and right, so the R (right) and L (left) in the word trade places

parts.note: to have reeled is to have twisted and staggered about

explanation.surface: Someone gave a nasty look after contorting and changing positions.
explanation.walkthrough: In REELED the R stands for right and the L for left; 'when swapping sides' exchanges those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to give a sly, lecherous or malicious glance, an unpleasant way of looking.

clue.text: Bulletin needs bit of punctuation — not a one-off

parts.note: COMMA without its A
unique = one of a kind

explanation.surface: A news notice that wants a comma added, not as a one-time fix.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'not a one-off' read as a phrase; split it so 'not a' works on COMMA and 'one-off' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An official statement issued to the press is a bulletin in the plain sense, and the word comes straight from French for 'communicated'.

clue.text: Has sprint legend cut energy?

indicators.note: cut means removed, so the energy letter is taken out of the sprinter's name

parts.note: Jesse Owens, the American sprinter who won four golds at the 1936 Olympics
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Asking whether a great sprinter has lost his zip.
explanation.walkthrough: Jesse Owens was the US track star of the 1936 Berlin Olympics; 'cut' drops the E that stands for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, which is what having it means.

clue.text: Turn a pair of taps, this produces water when you're boiling

definitions.text: this produces water when you're boiling

parts.note: spin = turn
as written
taps are labelled C (cold) and H (hot)

explanation.surface: Instructions for running water from two taps when you're overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You're boiling' sounds like feeling hot, but it means you are boiling the vegetable, which leaks a surprising amount of water into the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach wilts and releases lots of water when boiled.

clue.text: Worker who gives rise to loot?

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise to the top reads the word loot from the bottom upwards

parts.note: one who gives rise to something is its maker or creator

explanation.surface: Someone whose job makes them responsible for producing plunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, 'gives rise to' means creates; here 'rise to' reads LOOT upwards in this down clue, giving TOOL, and 'who gives' is the maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolmaker is a skilled tradesperson who makes and repairs tools, so a kind of worker.

clue.text: Nick will be married in Paris if up and fit

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the French word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: si is the French word for if
fit as an adjective means suitable, appropriate

explanation.surface: A man called Nick plans to marry in France if he is well enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name but is the verb to steal. 'in Paris' turns if into French SI, and 'up' reads it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is slang for to steal, and to misappropriate is to take dishonestly what belongs to another.

clue.text: Rocky bridge from Sting EP on piano's dividing old group

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the singer's name apart, with the record and piano letter set in the gap

parts.note: taken as written: the singer's name

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the record is set beside the piano letter

parts.note: taken as written: an extended-play record
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
the Rolling Stones, the veteran rock band, often called just the Stones

explanation.surface: A rock fan's tale of a Sting EP played on piano, set beside a classic band.
explanation.walkthrough: EP 'on' P (for piano) together divide STING to make STEPPING; then add the Stones. 'Rocky' looks like music talk but literally describes the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping stones are a row of stones laid across a stream so you can walk over, a bridge made of rock.

clue.text: Chap in race animated barmiest finish in marathon

indicators.note: animated means lively and in motion, so the letters are set moving

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of marathoN

explanation.surface: A man in a running race finishes the marathon in the wildest state of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' reads as a running race, but it means a people or tribe. Barmy is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribesman is a man belonging to a tribe, a race of people.

clue.text: I party less, having no need for insiders and stars

parts.note: as written
a do is a party

parts.words: less, having no need for insiders
parts.note: LESS with its inside letters ES dropped

explanation.surface: A would-be celebrity claims to go out less, needing no inside friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insiders' means the inner letters of the word just before it, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are stars, celebrities worshipped by fans.

clue.text: Level, leapt extraordinarily, followed by gold

indicators.note: followed by means the gold symbol comes after the rearranged letters
extraordinarily means in an unusual way, so the letters of leapt are rearranged

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An athlete jumped amazingly and won gold, steady at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' rearranges LEAPT to PLATE, and 'followed by' adds the chemical symbol for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a stage where things stay steady, as when progress levels off after rising.

clue.text: Combat uniform required in Military Police's preparation for conflict?

parts.note: war = combat

indicators.note: what is required in something has to go inside it

parts.note: the initials M and P of Military Police
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet, placed inside MP

explanation.surface: Battle fatigues are compulsory for military police getting ready for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combat uniform' is one phrase in the surface but splits in two. The question mark covers the stretch: a warm-up readies athletes for a contest, not literally a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-up is preparation before a contest, playfully called conflict here.

clue.text: Incite riots about Jamaican music genre, primarily for sport

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the Jamaican style
to run riot is to go wild, so the letters of incite plus one more are thrown into disorder
primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter of genre

parts.note: first letter of genre
ska is an upbeat Jamaican music style, forerunner of reggae

explanation.surface: A Jamaican music style accused of stirring up disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incite riots' reads as a phrase, but 'riots' is the anagram signal, taking the genre's first letter along with INCITE to give ICETING; 'about' wraps that round the Jamaican music.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating on ice is a recreational and competitive sport, including figure skating and speed skating.

clue.text: More than one troublemaker is surrounding person who's 16

indicators.note: what surrounds something goes round it

parts.note: as written
16 down is POLITICAL; an MP (Member of Parliament) is a political person, placed inside IS

explanation.surface: A roomful of troublemakers gathers round a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at 16 down, POLITICAL, so the person is a politician, MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are mischievous troublemakers, usually children.

clue.text: Vote to restrict CIA, it worked out of government

indicators.note: to restrict is to hold in, so the poll letters enclose the rest

parts.note: a poll is a vote

indicators.note: worked out means reshaped, so the letters of CIA and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballot meant to curb the spy agency succeeded and ousted the administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges CIA IT to ITICA, which POLL holds 'to restrict' it. 'out of government' reads as removed from power; the definition is only 'of government'.
explanation.definitionFit: Political means relating to the state and its affairs, the business of governing a country.

clue.text: Poor soul requesting pick-me-up, by the way?

definitions.meaning: read as someone low asking for a tonic; meant as someone asking to be picked up, given a lift
read as a throwaway aside; meant literally, standing by the road

explanation.surface: A sorry figure casually asking for a drink or tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick-me-up' reads as a tonic and 'by the way' as an aside; taken literally, the traveller asks to be picked up and waits beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch-hiker stands by the road asking passing drivers for a lift.

clue.text: Greens targeting drivers here? On the contrary

definitions.meaning: read as environmentalists going after motorists; greens and drivers are both golf words
swap the roles: drivers, the long-hitting clubs, target the greens

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners going after motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' suggests environmentalists and 'drivers' motorists; 'on the contrary' swaps the roles, and both words turn out to be golf terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf course is where drivers (clubs) send balls towards greens.

clue.text: Hoax Democrat used before November's doom?

parts.note: a con is a hoax or swindle
Dem. is the abbreviation for Democrat
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A fake Democrat spells disaster for the November elections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'November' suggests the US election month, but it only supplies the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom as a verb, to consign someone to an unhappy fate, is exactly what a court does when it condemns a prisoner.

clue.text: Stumble in tango, leading to endless tears

indicators.note: what leads to something comes before it

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO alphabet
RIPS (tears) without its last letter

explanation.surface: A dancer falls over mid-tango and it ends in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' are rips here, not crying; the surface's weeping is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: catching your foot and losing balance, as in a trip on the stairs.

clue.text: Tipsy choirmaster's embraces one disturbed

indicators.note: what embraces something holds it inside, so the answer sits within the words

parts.note: tiPSY CHOirmaster: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: A drunken choirmaster hugs a troubled chorister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embraces' reads as a hug, but it tells you the answer is held within the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho is, informally, a mentally disturbed person.

clue.text: They're mighty birds with a new stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside a bird

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
A plus N (new), stuffed inside TITS

explanation.surface: Some impressive birds come with a novel stuffing, as if for a roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' fits the birds-for-dinner picture, but it tells you AN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans are giants, people or things of great might.

clue.text: Spike in marriages sadly going west

indicators.note: the answer is held in the words that follow
on a map west is to the left, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: marrIAGES SAdly, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A rise in the number of weddings that end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' reads as a surge in numbers, but it is a pointed weapon. 'Going west' also hints at things going wrong, which suits the sad marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Killjoy needs good seat

parts.note: g = good
rump = backside, seat

explanation.surface: A spoilsport wants a comfortable chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' means the backside, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A grump, a sulky and bad-tempered person, is the kind of killjoy who spoils others' fun.

clue.text: Free trade, third reduced by 90 per cent

indicators.note: the third letter is a Roman numeral fifty; cut by ninety per cent it becomes five, the Roman numeral for five

parts.note: a sale is a piece of trade, an exchange of goods for money

explanation.surface: Open commerce where a third of the goods are almost entirely discounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third reduced by 90 per cent': the third letter of SALE is L, Roman 50, and cutting it by 90 per cent leaves 5, which is V in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone is to rescue them, which sets them free from danger.

clue.text: Hotel occupies particular special area

indicators.note: what occupies a place sits inside it

parts.note: nice = particular, fussy, as in a nice distinction
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet, placed inside NICE

explanation.surface: A hotel takes over an exclusive section of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The old sense of nice as precise or fastidious is what matches 'particular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A special area of interest or trade, as in a niche market, borrows the word for a recess in a wall.

clue.text: Disheartened over meeting date where fight took place

indicators.note: meeting means joining, so the two pieces are put together

parts.note: AGAIN (over, once more) with its middle letter A removed
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone crushed after a date recalls where a quarrel broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' means again, as in 'do it over'. Agincourt is the 1415 battle in northern France won by Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Agincourt was fought there in 1415.

clue.text: Something that gets under my skin? Huddles — they disrupt a party

parts.words: Something that gets under my skin?
parts.note: a splinter literally lodges under the skin
huddles are tight groups

explanation.surface: An irritating guest crowds people into cliques and spoils the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets under my skin' sounds like annoyance, but it is literal. 'Party' is a political party, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Splinter groups break away from a political party and divide it.
